Consumer Non-Cyclicals: The Consumer Non-Cyclicals sector posted a solid performance, ranking seventh out of fifteen sectors based on median price changes over the past month, and it outperformed the broader SGX index on the same metric. Four of the ten constituent companies recorded positive price moves, indicating that a minority of the names are driving the sector’s upside. This strength likely stems from the defensive nature of consumer staples, which tend to benefit from steady household spending even when broader market sentiment wavers. Current market health is also shaped by tourism rebound, shifts in consumer confidence, Singapore dollar fluctuations, recent regulatory adjustments to retail licensing, and input‑cost pressure from commodity price volatility.
Consumer Cyclicals: The Consumer Cyclicals sector, made up of 84 companies, slipped to 10th place out of 15 in the 30‑day median price‑change ranking, with its median move trailing the overall SGX median. Only 26 of the constituents posted a positive price change over the period, underscoring the breadth of weakness. This underperformance likely reflects dampened consumer spending as higher borrowing costs and lingering supply‑chain constraints curb discretionary purchases, while a slower tourism rebound and tighter regulatory scrutiny weigh on retail and leisure earnings. Additional market‑specific pressures include elevated interest rates, weaker consumer confidence, and tighter credit conditions.
Transportation & Logistics: The Transportation & Logistics sector, comprising eight listed firms, ranked second out of fifteen sectors for median price change over the past 30 days, allowing it to outpace the overall SGX median movement. Despite only three companies posting positive returns, the sector’s aggregate momentum was buoyed by a surge in regional freight demand, easing port congestion and continued e‑commerce expansion that lifted volume expectations. At the same time, tighter fuel pricing, new emissions‑related regulations, ongoing infrastructure upgrades, and a tight labor market are unique conditions shaping the health of the logistics segment on the Singapore index. These dynamics together explain why the sector’s median price change has been stronger than the broader market.
Healthcare: The Healthcare sector, with 40 listed firms, slipped to 12th out of 15 in the 30‑day median price‑change ranking, and its median move lagged behind the SGX overall median. Only nine companies posted a positive price change, underscoring the breadth of the decline. This under‑performance may stem from tighter regulatory scrutiny, reduced reimbursement rates, and lingering uncertainties around post‑pandemic vaccine demand, all of which can suppress investor sentiment. Additional Singapore‑specific factors currently influencing the market include recent policy adjustments to healthcare subsidies, an aging demographic pressure on service providers, shifts in biotech funding incentives, and heightened foreign‑exchange volatility affecting import‑dependent medical supplies.
Properties & Real Estate: The Properties & Real Estate sector, comprising 53 listed companies, ranked eighth out of fifteen in median price change over the past month. It also posted a higher median gain than the broader SGX, indicating stronger momentum across the sector. Only nine firms recorded positive price moves, suggesting that the sector’s outperformance is driven by a relatively small group of high‑performing assets. Renewed demand for office space as firms adopt hybrid work models, stable rental yields and recent government incentives for property development are likely contributors to the stronger price dynamics. Singapore‑specific factors that can uniquely affect market health include tightening loan‑to‑value limits, upcoming land‑sale exercises and shifts in foreign investor sentiment.
Energy: The Energy sector, comprising 23 companies, ranked ninth out of fifteen sectors for median price change over the past 30 days and managed to outpace the overall SGX median movement. Despite the sector‑wide gain, only five firms posted positive price changes, indicating that the uplift was driven by a few strong performers. This outperformance likely reflects a rebound in global oil prices, heightened regional demand for LNG, and recent adjustments to carbon‑related regulations that have favored traditional energy producers. Current market health is also being shaped by factors such as regional LNG supply constraints, changes in carbon tax policy, fluctuations in crude oil inventories, and shifts in renewable energy subsidies.
Utilities: The Utilities sector, comprising 13 listed firms, ranked last (15 of 15) in median price change over the past month, and its median move lagged the overall SGX median. Only two companies posted a positive price change, underscoring the breadth of the decline. This underperformance likely reflects the sector’s heightened sensitivity to regulatory rate adjustments, volatile fuel costs, evolving climate‑policy mandates, delayed infrastructure investment cycles, and grid‑reliability concerns that are uniquely shaping Singapore’s utilities market today.
Consumer Defensive: The Consumer Defensive sector, comprising 30 listed companies, slipped to 13th place out of 15 in the 30‑day median price‑change ranking, with its median move trailing the overall SGX median. Only seven firms posted a positive price change over the period, leaving the majority in negative territory. The underperformance likely reflects subdued domestic consumption, higher input and commodity costs, and lingering supply‑chain constraints that have squeezed profit margins. Current market‑specific factors influencing the sector’s health in the Singapore index include weaker consumer confidence, a stronger local currency, tighter credit conditions, recent regulatory adjustments affecting retail pricing, and lingering tourism slowdown.
Financial Services: Out of fifteen SGX sectors, Financial Services ranked fourth in median price change over the past month, with nine of its twenty‑nine constituents posting gains. The sector’s median uplift outpaced the broader SGX, suggesting that investors are rewarding the group’s exposure to rising interest margins and resilient fee‑based income. Current market conditions that can uniquely sway the sector include the central bank’s policy stance, regional banking stress, regulatory reforms, evolving fintech competition, and shifts in capital flows.
Communication Services: The Communication Services sector topped the SGX sector rankings, landing first out of fifteen based on median price change over the past month. Six of the fifteen listed companies posted positive price moves, underscoring the breadth of the rally. The outperformance relative to the broader SGX likely reflects heightened demand for digital advertising, accelerated 5G network roll‑outs, and a rebound in regional tourism that boosted telecom and media revenues. Current market health is also shaped by the regulatory environment, consumer spending trends, telecom infrastructure upgrades, advertising revenue growth, and regional economic integration.
Basic Materials: The Basic Materials sector, comprising 36 listed companies, secured the third‑best rank out of fifteen sectors for median price change over the past 30 days, outpacing the broader SGX market. Eleven of the constituents posted positive price moves, indicating that roughly one‑third of the sector benefited from recent market dynamics. This relative strength likely reflects a combination of rising global commodity prices, heightened regional construction activity, recent regulatory adjustments to mining permits, currency fluctuations affecting export margins, and ongoing supply‑chain constraints that uniquely impact Singapore’s material‑focused firms. Together, these factors have helped lift the sector’s median price performance above the overall exchange trend.
Infrastructures: Out of fifteen SGX sectors, the Infrastructures sector ranked 11th, with its median price change lagging behind the overall market median over the past 30 days. The sector comprises seven listed companies, of which only two posted positive price moves during the same period, underscoring the weak momentum. The underperformance may stem from tighter government capital allocation, delays in large‑scale project approvals, higher construction material costs and regional supply‑chain bottlenecks that have weighed on investor sentiment. These market‑specific pressures, combined with the sector’s lower median return, explain why its price trajectory trails the broader index.
REIT: The REIT sector lagged behind the broader market, ranking 14th out of 15 based on median price changes over the past month. Its median price change was below the SGX overall median, and only five of the 42 constituent companies posted gains in the last 30 days. This weakness likely reflects the impact of higher interest rates, tighter credit conditions, subdued tourism demand, recent regulatory adjustments, and an influx of new REIT listings, all of which can uniquely pressure Singapore’s REIT market health.
Industrials: The Industrials sector, with 127 listed companies, ranked sixth out of fifteen in median price change over the past month, outpacing the broader SGX. Forty‑two firms posted a positive price move, indicating that roughly a third of the sector benefitted from the rally. This outperformance likely reflects heightened demand for infrastructure projects, easing of regional shipping bottlenecks and a rebound in freight rates, which together lifted earnings expectations for many industrial operators. Current market health is further shaped by global supply‑chain constraints, regional infrastructure spending plans, freight‑rate volatility, regulatory reforms affecting heavy equipment imports, and oil‑price fluctuations.
Technology: Among the fifteen SGX sectors, the Technology sector ranked fifth in median price change over the past month, with 58 listed firms and 19 posting gains. Its median rise outpaced the overall SGX market, reflecting strong investor appetite for tech exposure. The uplift can be linked to robust regional demand for digital transformation, continued government incentives for innovation, and easing of supply‑chain bottlenecks in semiconductor components. Additional market‑specific drivers such as elevated venture capital activity, favorable foreign exchange conditions for export‑oriented tech firms, and a supportive regulatory environment also bolster the sector’s health.
